tagline: Leading provider of life insurance, annuities and retirement solutions
hero_kpi_rationale: Financial strength ratings constitute a critical indicator for LNC, an insurance company, as they directly impact the ability to market products, customer confidence and financing costs. Maintenance above the BBB-/Baa3 threshold is essential to avoid termination clauses in derivative and acquisition contracts.

kpis.name: Financial Strength Ratings
kpis.explanation: Assessment of an insurance company's capacity to pay claims and other obligations, assigned by rating agencies.
kpis.description: Ratings assigned by S&P and Moody's (critical thresholds: BBB-/Baa3 for LNC, BBB+/Baa1 for certain acquisition agreements). A downgrade may trigger termination clauses in derivative contracts.
kpis.signal: Impacts customer confidence, product marketing and financing costs.

kpis.name: Equity Market Risk Exposure
kpis.explanation: Risk of financial loss due to fluctuations in securities or stock market indices affecting commission revenues on variable products.
kpis.description: Revenues from variable annuities and variable life insurance depend as a percentage on the value of underlying assets. A significant market decline reduces commission revenues and may result in substantial client withdrawals.
kpis.signal: Indicates revenue and asset sensitivity to stock market movements.

kpis.name: Interest Rate Risk
kpis.explanation: Risk of financial loss linked to interest rate changes affecting profitability, capital and investment portfolio value.
kpis.description: Sustained interest rate increases can reduce the value of the bond investment portfolio, decrease profitability and result in increased contract surrenders by policyholders, affecting the capital position.
kpis.signal: A rate increase may impair profitability and increase contract surrenders and withdrawals.

kpis.name: Credit Risk
kpis.explanation: Risk of financial loss related to a debtor's or counterparty's inability to honor its obligations.
kpis.description: LNC is exposed to default risk from its counterparties on investments (bonds, mortgage loans) and derivative contracts. Management measures are in place but risk remains in case of economic slowdown.
kpis.signal: Reflects exposure through bond portfolios, mortgage loans and derivative contracts.

kpis.name: Total Investments
kpis.explanation: Total market value of portfolio investments.
kpis.description: Total investments as of December 31, 2025, including fixed income securities, equities, derivative investments and other investments, with a book value of 138,908 million USD.
kpis.signal: Reflects the size of the asset portfolio supporting insurance obligations.

kpis.name: Fixed Maturity Securities
kpis.explanation: Portfolio of bond securities classified as available-for-sale assets.
kpis.description: U.S. government, foreign, municipal, corporate bonds and mortgage-backed securities, with a total book value of 93,448 million USD as of December 31, 2025.
kpis.signal: Represents the core of the investment income portfolio and is sensitive to interest rate and credit risks.

kpis.name: Mortgage Loans
kpis.explanation: Portfolio of mortgage loans secured by real property.
kpis.description: Mortgage loans on real property with a book value of 22,472 million USD as of December 31, 2025, net of credit loss provisions.
kpis.signal: Significant component of investment portfolio returns, exposed to real estate credit risk.

kpis.name: Stockholders Equity
kpis.explanation: Total value of net assets attributable to shareholders.
kpis.description: Total stockholders equity of the parent company as of December 31, 2025, including preferred stock, common stock, retained earnings and accumulated other comprehensive results, totaling 10,906 million USD.
kpis.signal: Reflects financial strength and capacity to absorb market shocks.

risks.title: Equity market volatility impacting revenues
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly mentions that revenues from variable life insurance and annuity products are linked to equity market values. A significant decline can reduce revenues and trigger withdrawals, directly affecting profitability. Sensitivity is quantified, indicating material importance.

risks.title: Interest rate risk on profitability and capital
risks.score_rationale: Rising interest rates are explicitly cited as potentially negatively affecting profitability, capital position and investment portfolio value. This may also increase contract surrenders. The language used ('may negatively affect') suggests serious concern.

risks.title: Credit risk on investment portfolios
risks.score_rationale: Credit risk is clearly defined as the risk of financial loss linked to a debtor's or counterparty's inability to honor its obligations. The company is exposed through its investments (bonds, mortgage loans) and derivatives. Although management measures are in place, risk remains, particularly in economic slowdowns.

risks.title: Counterparty risk on derivative instruments
risks.score_rationale: The text details credit risk exposure from counterparties in derivative contracts. The company depends on derivative dealers' capacity to honor their obligations. Although exposure limits and rating requirements are applied, counterparty default risk exists.

risks.title: Foreign exchange risk on foreign investments
risks.score_rationale: The risk of financial loss due to currency rate variations is identified for investments not denominated in US dollars. Although the company uses derivatives for hedging, unhedged positions exist, though their amount is relatively small (less than 10 million USD in total).

risks.title: Risk related to insurance products and actuarial assumptions
risks.score_rationale: Variable life insurance and annuity contracts are exposed to risks related to changes in pricing assumptions, including non-market actuarial assumptions. These risks are managed through product design, hedging and reinsurance, but their potential impact is highlighted.

risks.title: Risk of solvency rating downgrade
risks.score_rationale: A downgrade below BBB-/Baa3 for LNC or BBB+/Baa1 for LNL would trigger termination clauses in derivative contracts and certain acquisition agreements, affecting overall liquidity. A downgrade could also compromise product marketing and creditor relations.

ai_positioning.summary: LNC does not mention artificial intelligence in its 10-K/20-F report.
